title: Recalibrate the scoped lane's serial-runtime budget against real lane history
description:
Proposed by sase-gj.2 and sase-gj.7 while the diff-scoped lane latency epic was in flight; corroborated with new measurements by the sase-gj land agent.

FULL_LANE_WALL_SECONDS (tests/_test_selection_health.py) is 232.0s and doubles as the default for SASE_TEST_SELECTION_MAX_SERIAL_SECONDS, i.e. the crossover at which RULE_SERIAL_BUDGET_EXCEEDED escalates or hands a selection to the middle gear. It was set from a single 2026-08-06 measurement at 28 workers. Three later same-day timed full lanes on the same host came in well under it: 159.0s (sase-gj.7, 26,497 tests), and 139.95s during the sase-gj land verification (26,496 passed / 7 skipped). If that holds, the budget is ~1.5x looser than the real crossover, so runs that should escalate or engage the gear stay serial.

sase-gj.2 separately proposed correcting the duration table for parallel contention: per-test seconds recorded on the 28-worker full lane over-state an isolated serial run (hand samples: 12 slow ACE files estimated 338.8s vs 298.2s actual, 1.14x; 11 selection-test files 26.4s vs 11.8s, 2.2x). That measurement does NOT reproduce against real lane history, which is the evidence sase-gj.2 wanted and could not get at the time: the health store does record manifest["selected"], timings.estimated_serial_seconds, and the run duration together on every non-escalated schema>=6 record. Estimate/actual over the 4 such serial records now in the store is mean 0.90x (0.74, 0.91, 0.92, 1.03) — the estimate slightly UNDER-states real lane wall clock, because the lane duration also carries pytest startup and the contract set. n=4 is thin; the two measurements disagree and need more samples to settle.

Also of note: the merged table total moved from 4268.4s over 2346 files (sase-gj.1) to 3239.0s over 2370 files (land), so the table itself is load-sensitive between recordings.

Scope: take repeated timed full-lane measurements, pull estimate-vs-duration pairs from the accumulated store, decide whether FULL_LANE_WALL_SECONDS should move and whether the per-file table needs a contention correction, and update the constants, their "measured, deliberately constant" docstrings, and docs/development.md with the new numbers. Do not change the constant on a single sample; that is what produced this task.

title: Flaky test_installing_prunes_the_cache_to_the_keep_limit: cached_baselines mtime sort has no tie-break
description:
Found by the sase-gj land agent while running `just check-full` on master at 0de333e5d (plus a Justfile comment edit). Not caused by that epic.

FAILURE (full parallel lane, 28 workers, 1 failed / 26,496 passed / 7 skipped in 139.95s):

  tests/test_install_coverage_contexts_tool.py::test_installing_prunes_the_cache_to_the_keep_limit
  >       assert remaining[0].sha == _head(repo)
  E       AssertionError: assert 0000000000000000000000000000000000000003 == cc2e180224ba34abce1063410100858a67e0e00f

Passes 4/4 in isolation (`pytest tests/test_install_coverage_contexts_tool.py`, with and without -p no:randomly), so it is load-sensitive, not order-dependent.

PRE-EXISTING, not new: the same node ID appears in `just selection-health` as a false negative, failing in the full-lane record 20260806T201818Z-48bd0009ebdc-1524219-full-run.json at head 48bd0009ebdc, which `git merge-base --is-ancestor 48bd0009e cc241fae0` confirms predates the sase-gj epic.

SUSPECTED ROOT CAUSE (diagnosed by reading, not reproduced under load): tests/_test_selection_contexts.py:234 sorts with `baselines.sort(key=lambda baseline: _mtime(baseline.path), reverse=True)` and `_mtime` (line 238) returns `path.stat().st_mtime` — a float, whose precision at the current epoch is ~238ns — with no secondary sort key. `list.sort` is stable, so an mtime tie falls back to `directory.iterdir()` order, which is filesystem-arbitrary. The test writes four dummy databases and then installs the real one, and tools/install_coverage_contexts uses `shutil.copy2` + `Path.replace` (lines 177-178), both of which preserve the SOURCE mtime — so the installed baseline inherits repo/.coverage`s mtime rather than getting a fresh one, narrowing the gap that has to survive the float rounding.

Scope: confirm the mechanism under load, then either give cached_baselines a deterministic tie-break (st_mtime_ns, and a name tie-break under that) or make the test set explicit mtimes. Related but distinct from sase-g9, which changed resolve_baseline to rank by breadth and deliberately left cached_baselines on mtime order for pruning; this is about that mtime order being non-deterministic on ties, not about which ordering pruning should use.

title: sase/memory/build_and_run.md still claims the diff-scoped lane "takes no suite-gate lease"
description:
Found by the sase-gj land agent. Caused by sase-gj.3 (the middle gear), which made the claim false and did not update the always-loaded memory.

Before sase-gj.3, `just check`'s scoped test lane was serial and took no suite-gate lease at all. The middle gear changed that: when RULE_SERIAL_BUDGET_EXCEEDED is the only reason a selection would escalate, tests/_test_selection_gear.engage_scoped_gear() builds a real `WorkerTokenLease` against `gate_directory()` and calls `try_acquire()`, then runs the selection at the granted width. The lease is bounded (ceiling 4) and strictly non-blocking — a refused grant escalates rather than queues — so the promise that actually matters to agents ("never waits behind another agent's run") still holds, but "takes no suite-gate lease" is now false whenever the gear engages.

STALE IN (both lines carry it):
  sase/memory/build_and_run.md:13  — `just check` comment block: "test lane that takes no suite-gate lease"
  sase/memory/build_and_run.md:27  — "...static import-graph closure and takes no suite-gate lease."

Those propagate verbatim into the generated provider shims AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, OPENCODE.md, and QWEN.md (lines 20 and 34 of each), so every agent in this repo currently reads the false claim in its always-loaded Tier 1 memory.

ALREADY FIXED, for reference on the wording to match:
  docs/development.md:60 — "The scoped run is serial (`-n 1`) unless the middle gear below wins it a small lease, and it never queues behind other agents' runs either way." (sase-gj.7)
  Justfile — the `test-scoped` and `check` recipe comments, corrected by the sase-gj land agent.

Scope: correct both lines in sase/memory/build_and_run.md, then run `sase memory init` to regenerate AGENTS.md and the provider shims. NOTE FOR THE ASSIGNEE: editing sase/memory/*.md requires the user's explicit permission in the conversation that does the work — per CLAUDE.md, authorization recorded in a bead description does not count. The land agent left this as a task for exactly that reason rather than editing memory without permission. Once the user asks for the edit, running `sase memory init` afterwards is mandatory and needs no separate approval.

Intentional divergence preserved per the plan: "Google Chat should lean
on threads and dot commands; Telegram should keep button-heavy
workflows." The Telegram retry path is button-driven; the gchat retry
path is typed.

Deferred follow-ups documented in retired chat plugin/ROADMAP.md:
- Reactions on plan approvals (gchat-only UX)
- Streaming / draft API limitations (Google Chat platform constraints)
- .retry polish — no-arg .retry list, recovered-prompt preview
- Dot-command argument hints (e.g. --filter <substring>)

No equivalent ROADMAP exists in sase-telegram and none was added in
this phase — the gaps relative to gchat are deliberate platform-specific
divergences, not parity debt.
